title: Consolidate preserves template value instead of summarizing
query: We have a bloated skill SKILL.md with repeated rationale, a required Todo List, a Skill Signature, and a few rare examples. Use consolidate to make it shorter.
reference_points: Finds or names the owning skill template before rewriting
Slices the skill into sections or units before deciding actions
Preserves required first-load behavior such as trigger, signature, todo path, gates, proof, and output
Classifies units as keep, merge, rewrite, move, delete, promote, demote, or defer
Moves rare examples or branch-specific detail only when reference routing remains explicit
Runs or requires a loss check rather than claiming shorter is better
Routes material skill edits to skill-maintenance checks or review instead of self-approving
notes: Protects the primitive from becoming a generic summary instruction.

title: Consolidate separates hard constraints from value judgment
query: Consolidate a feature registry to fewer rows, but preserve FEAT IDs and generated-registry compatibility. Can we just sort by usage and delete the bottom half?
reference_points: Treats preserve_ids and generated compatibility as hard constraints
Rejects deleting solely by low usage or row count
Names a value function that includes proof, routing, reuse, memory, and user value
Requires source-owner or consumer checks before retire/delete decisions
Returns keep/merge/retire or handoff decisions with evidence
Requires validator or generated-output proof before claiming completion
notes: Catches the parameter/value-function split for registry-like targets.

title: Consolidate routes gotchas to the right owner surface
query: A skill has twenty gotchas, some are repeated runtime failures, some are stale one-off warnings, and some are examples. Consolidate them.
reference_points: Inventories gotchas as individual units before rewriting
Promotes repeated runtime failures into qa_checklist.md, eval_task.json, or SKILL.md gates when reusable
Deletes or demotes stale one-off warnings only after checking loss risk
Moves examples to references when they are useful but not every-invocation guardrails
Keeps concise gotchas only when they prevent common wrong behavior
Includes a loss check and proof or review route for material skill changes
notes: Exercises consolidate across gotchas, checklist, eval, and reference placement.
